context: Current closing price of Procter & Gamble (PG): $165.40 USD as of 2026-11-06.
justification_text:
My point estimates for all horizons – one day, one week, and one month – consistently settled at 165.4. This uniformity primarily reflects an assumption that the current observed value, or a very recent short-term average, serves as the most reliable baseline for future expectations. In the absence of strong immediate signals suggesting a significant upward or downward trend, the forecast essentially posits that the immediate future will largely resemble the present, acting as a stable anchor point from which future deviations might occur. This approach is common when historical data doesn't reveal strong, persistent trends that are expected to continue or accelerate.

The varying widths of the confidence intervals directly reflect the accumulation of uncertainty over time. For the one-day horizon, the interval is relatively tight, accounting for typical daily fluctuations and noise. As we extend to one week and then one month, the intervals progressively widen. This expansion is driven by the inherent volatility of the underlying metric; the longer the time frame, the greater the potential for random variations, minor shifts in underlying conditions, or unexpected fluctuations to compound. Essentially, the future becomes progressively less predictable the further out we attempt to look, necessitating broader ranges to capture 90% of potential outcomes.

While these confidence intervals aim to capture the vast majority of probable outcomes based on historical patterns, certain high-impact, low-probability events could certainly push actual results beyond these stated ranges. These "tail risks" might include significant macroeconomic shocks, such as an unexpected recession, rapid inflation, or sudden shifts in central bank monetary policy. Geopolitical instability, major technological disruptions impacting the relevant industry, or unforeseen regulatory changes could also introduce substantial volatility. Any event that fundamentally alters the prevailing market conditions or the underlying drivers of the forecasted value, and was not implicitly accounted for in the historical data or short-term trends informing the model, holds the potential to create outcomes far outside the anticipated 90% range.
